message: **The Kubernetes Gateway controller publishes `sb.yml` whole or not at all.** It rendered the document straight over the existing file, so a controller pod killed between the truncate and the write left a partial config on the shared volume, and a data plane restarting on it could not boot. Each publish now writes a temporary file in the same directory, flushes it, renames it into place, and syncs the directory, so a reader opens either the previous complete document or the new one. A publish that fails leaves the last good document byte for byte intact and no temporary behind, and a mode an operator set on the published file survives the next reconcile. Rename atomicity and `fsync` durability are the filesystem's promise, so on an NFS-backed volume this is as strong as the server underneath it. See [docs/gateway-api.md](docs/gateway-api.md).
